key: must:I45a:Woman curly black bob and yellow raincoat; man white beard and blue coat
symptom: Woman curly black bob and yellow raincoat; man white beard and blue coat

whys.why: Why do the woman and the man in both videos not have the curly black bob, yellow raincoat, white beard and blue coat?
whys.because: The prompts the assistant sent to create_video_from_text never mention any of these traits. The model drew what the prompt asked for.
whys.evidence: old calls.jsonl: the prompt says 'an elderly man… a young woman' and nothing else about their looks; grader: 'long straight dark hair… clean-shaven'. new calls.jsonl: the prompt says 'elderly man in a grey coat… young woman in a mustard scarf'; grader: 'gray coat and mustard scarf… no beard'. The output matches the invented prompt.

whys.why: Why did the prompts not contain the character traits?
whys.because: The assistant never got the traits. The stupid user's only content message was 'make a video about a kind gesture at a park bench'. The assistant then invented the cast and the story (sandwich/coffee, tea cups), and also the clothing in new.
whys.evidence: chat.json messages[0] = 'make a video about a kind gesture at a park bench'. The traits exist only in the persona bank under 'Characters'. old state: no user reply before the call.

whys.why: Why did the assistant not get the traits from the user, when the bank has them and the persona answers plain-word questions?
whys.because: Neither build asked who is in the video or what happens. Old asked nothing and generated at once. New asked only about length, platform/aspect, sound and on-screen words.
whys.evidence: old calls.jsonl: create_video_from_text is the first call, with no question. new calls.jsonl: plan_request returned questions only for seconds, aspect, sound and exact_words, then ready:true. The user answered each plain question from the bank ('15 sec, no sound', 'no words').

whys.why: Why did new's plan_request not ask about the content?
whys.because: plan_request took the vague one-line subject as a complete value (source=user). Its gap check covers only format slots, so a subject with no characters or story events never sets ready=false.
whys.evidence: tools-new.json plan_request description: 'do not guess shape, length, sound or on-screen words'. It says nothing about subject detail. Its output marked subject 'a kind gesture at a park bench' as source user and returned ready:true after the format questions.

whys.why: Why did old not ask either?
whys.because: Old has no planning or clarification tool. With nothing prompting a question, the assistant followed its default and filled the open subject with its own invented story.
whys.evidence: old calls.jsonl: the only calls are create_video_from_text (after it rejected model 'default') and wait_for_video_project. There is no planning step.

result.axiom: When the user's request names only a theme ('a kind gesture at a park bench'), neither build has a step that finds missing characters or story. New's plan_request checks only format slots (length, aspect, sound, words) and marks a thin subject as given. Old has no check at all. So the assistant invents the cast instead of asking a plain question the stupid user could answer from the bank.
result.fix: In plan_request (new, and the same idea added to old's tool descriptions), mark a subject as missing when it names no concrete characters or events, and return one plain-words question such as 'Who is in it, what do they look like, and what happens?'. Add a description rule: 'do not invent people, their looks or story events the user did not give'.
